Subject: SIG-lite onboarding: scope questions + next steps

Hi Elena / James —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and a short list of clarifying questions so we can route the appropriate SIG/CAIQ sections to our security team. I've attached a SIG-lite template (PDF) and a one-page vendor scope matrix for your convenience.

High-level from the call: FinServe will evaluate Redwood for a customer-facing document-generation feature (PII redaction and content moderation). Primary asks are SOC 2 status, GDPR controls for EU data residency, and whether we can support a HIPAA-compliant configuration for a pilot.

Questions we need answers to before we start the questionnaire:
- Scope: Will FinServe route production traffic through Redwood hosted API, or will you require a Private (VPC) deployment for the initial pilot? (this affects data access controls)
- Data types: Is the pilot expected to process PHI? If yes, please identify the categories (names, medical identifiers, claim numbers, notes).
- Residency: Any strict EU residency requirement for the pilot, or is multi-region acceptable?
- Evidence: Do you have a preferred format for evidence (SOC 2 PDF, interception logs, encryption config screenshots)?
- Third-party encryption: Do you require customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) or is provider-managed encryption acceptable for the pilot?

Next steps I propose:
1) FinServe confirms the three items above (scope, PHI yes/no, residency).
2) We return a prefilled SIG-lite with fields we can complete (we can fill standard answers for SOC 2/PCI where applicable).
3) Laura will run a short technical follow-up to clarify dataflow and caching (should take ~30 minutes).

Attachments: SIG-lite-template.pdf (our prefillable), vendor_scope_matrix.xlsx (scope matrix).

If the items above look right, can you confirm by EOD Monday 6/1 and we'll get the prefilled back to you the same day?

Thanks,

Hi Sergio / Monica / Laura —

Thanks for the recap. Short answers below; happy to expand. I'm attaching our internal security overview PDF that summarizes our compliance baseline.

- Scope: For the pilot we prefer Redwood hosted API (no VPC) initially, with the option to move to Private (VPC) if we proceed to a production contract.
- Data types: The pilot will NOT include PHI. We will test with redacted PII (names, emails). No medical identifiers.
- Residency: We'd like processing to stay within the US for the pilot; EU residency not required right now.
- Evidence: SOC 2 PDF is ideal; screenshots are fine for config items. A Doc/Drive link for longer artifacts works too.
- KMS: Provider-managed encryption is acceptable for pilot; we will request KMS only if we move to production.

Attached: FinServe_Security_Overview.pdf — high level of our controls and risk acceptance.

We can confirm by EOD Monday 6/1 as requested. Also — two quick clarifying items for Laura and Monica:
1) Do you have an expected retention policy for cached prompt/response data? (we map this to our data retention
policy)
2) Is there a simple list of required control families you need answered for this pilot (e.g., encryption in transit, access reviews, logging)?

Happy to schedule Laura's technical call next week; James and I are available Wed/Thu mornings ET.

Best,
Elena

FinServe Inc.

Elena / Team —

Thanks for the quick answers and for the overview doc. A couple short clarifications from a technical POV so we scope the SIG correctly:

- Retention: Our default hosted retention for request/response caching is 30 days; we can request a shortened retention window down to 0 days for pilot accounts (effectively no persistent cache) — would FinServe prefer 0 days for the pilot?
- Logging: We can supply request/response metadata (timestamps, request IDs) for audit purposes but we do not include full request payload in the standard audit logs unless explicitly configured; is metadata sufficient for your audit team for now?
- Encryption: All in-transit and at-rest encryption is standard; provider-managed KMS uses AES-256 with rotating keys. If you want customer-managed KMS for production we'll outline the integration steps.

If you confirm retention=0 days and that metadata-only logging is acceptable for pilot, I'll mark those fields in the SIG-lite prefill. Also let us know any additional control families to prioritize (e.g., data classification, access reviews).

Happy to take the Wed/Thu morning slot — send a calendar invite and we'll lock it.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
